bear.writtenAnchor: Coca-Cola's filed decade shows a top line that barely grew: 41.9bn in FY2016 against 47.9bn in FY2025, a 1.5% window CAGR, with outright declines in FY2017, FY2018 and FY2020 (H:revenue). The bear case assumes the recent step-up is mostly pricing that fades, volumes stay flat in developed markets, and currency and refranchising keep reported revenue growing about 2% a year. Margin gives back the FY2025 peak and settles near the FY2023-FY2024 zone, where impairment and legal charges pulled operating margin to 21.2% (H:margin). Net reinvestment runs above the filed median as capex continues its climb from 1,177m in FY2020 to 2,112m in FY2025 while D&A falls to 1,050m (H:capex), and each new dollar earns 10% \u2014 below the 9% discount rate plus moat credit, i.e. growth that barely pays for itself. Share count drifts up slightly with stock compensation of roughly 279m a year and no buyback disclosure in the supplied sources (H:cashflow).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The filed nine-year window CAGR is 1.5%, with declines in FY2017, FY2018 and FY2020, so a 2% constant rate assumes the recent acceleration fades back toward the long-run filed trend (H:revenue). It sits well inside the filed single-year range of -13.5% to 17.1%.

operatingMargin.text: Operating margin has swung from 20.7% in FY2016 to 28.7% in FY2025 and fell to 21.2% as recently as FY2024, so 24% assumes the FY2025 peak is not held and the average of the weaker recent years prevails (H:margin). This is inside the filed range and above its floor.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Capex has risen from 1,177m in FY2020 to 2,112m in FY2025 while D&A fell from 1,536m to 1,050m, so net reinvestment runs above the 1.4% filed median; 2.5% of revenue assumes that widening gap persists without buying much growth (H:capex).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Filed ROIC fell to 13.6% in FY2024 even on the 21% statutory tax rate, and incremental return on new capital is not disclosed; 10% assumes new dollars earn below the 9% terminal-plus-no-credit bar applied to the bear case.

shareCount.text: Operating cash flow fell to 6805m in FY2024 and 7408m in FY2025 while stock compensation ran 279m, so in a weak case buybacks only offset dilution and the diluted count is unchanged. (1× today's diluted count)

base.writtenAnchor: The base case takes the business as the latest filings describe it: FY2025 revenue 47,941m with operating income 13,762m, a 28.7% margin, and a trailing twelve months of 49,284m after a quarter ended 2026-04-03 that grew 12.1% on the year (H:revenue, H:margin, H:quarter). That recent momentum is treated as partly durable but not extrapolated: growth is set at 4.5%, above the 1.5% nine-year window CAGR but far below the 12.1% latest quarter and well inside the filed single-year range (H:revenue, H:quarter). Margin holds at 27.5%, between the FY2019-FY2021 band of about 27% and the FY2025 peak, on the view that the FY2024 dip reflected charges rather than the underlying mix (H:margin). Returns on new capital are set at 15%, inside the 13.6%-16.1% filed ROIC band (H:returns), fading by year 10 to 12% \u2014 the 9% rate plus a wide-moat credit the filed returns support. Net reinvestment of 1.8% of revenue sits just above the 1.4% filed median, reflecting the capex uptrend (H:capex), and share count is held flat.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: Revenue grew from 43,004m in FY2022 to 47,941m in FY2025 and the quarter ended 2026-04-03 was up 12.1% year on year, so 4.5% sits above the 1.5% window CAGR but discounts most of the recent quarter's pace (H:revenue, H:quarter). It is comfortably inside the filed single-year range.

operatingMargin.text: Margin was 27.1%-27.3% in FY2019-FY2020 and 28.7% in FY2025, with the 21.2% FY2024 reading an outlier against that band, so 27.5% is close to the filed recent norm and below the current 28.7% (H:margin).

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Median capex less depreciation has been 1.4% of revenue over ten years; 1.6% allows for the recent capex drift to 2,112m against D&A of 1,050m.

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Disclosed ROIC ran 13.6%-16.1% over FY2023-FY2025 at the statutory tax rate; 15% is inside that band, below 1.5x the 16.1% best filed return, and above the 12.0% wide-moat terminal return.

shareCount.text: Stock compensation is small, 279m in FY2025 against operating cash flow of 7408m, leaving room for modest net repurchases that trim the count about 2%. (0.98× today's diluted count)

bull.writtenAnchor: The bull case reads the quarter ended 2026-04-03 \u2014 revenue 12,472m, up 12.1%, trailing twelve months 49,284m \u2014 as the start of a faster stretch of pricing plus volume in developing markets, and holds revenue growth at 6.5% for five years, still well inside the filed single-year range that reached 17.1% (H:quarter, H:revenue). The refranchised, concentrate-heavy model is assumed to keep margin at 29.5%, roughly where FY2025's 28.7% landed and just above the top of the filed range (H:margin). Capital intensity stays light: net reinvestment of 1.4% of revenue, matching the filed median, as D&A of about 1.0bn offsets much of the 2.1bn capex (H:capex). New capital earns 19%, above the 16.1% best filed ROIC but inside the allowed 1.5x limit on the strength of a high-return, asset-light system (H:returns), fading to a 13.5% terminal return. Share count falls about 3% as cash flow comfortably covers stock compensation of roughly 279m (H:cashflow).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The quarter ended 2026-04-03 grew 12.1% on the year to 12,472m with trailing twelve months of 49,284m against FY2025's 47,941m, so 6.5% assumes roughly half that pace persists (H:quarter, H:revenue). It remains far inside the filed single-year high of 17.1%.

operatingMargin.text: FY2025 operating margin was 28.7%, the top of the filed range; 29.5% is within five points above that filed high and assumes continued pricing and concentrate mix.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Net reinvestment at the filed median of 1.4% of revenue reflects a system where 2,112m of FY2025 capex is largely matched over time by D&A averaging well above 1bn (H:capex).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: Best filed ROIC is 16.1% (FY2025); 19% is below 1.5x that figure and above the 13.5% bull terminal return, reflecting the low capital intensity of a franchise model where capex has never exceeded 2.3bn.

shareCount.text: At operating cash flow levels nearer the 12625m of FY2021 and with stock compensation only a few hundred million a year, net buybacks could reduce the diluted count by about 4%. (0.96× today's diluted count)

moatAnchor.text: Intangible assets — the brand and concentrate franchise system. Returns on invested capital of 13.6%-16.1% in every year disclosed, earned on operating margins of 24.7%-28.7% with capex of only about 2bn on revenue near 48bn, are the signature of pricing power from brands rather than deployed capital. The 12.0% wide-moat terminal return stays below every filed ROIC.

constantsAnchor.text: No company tax-rate disclosure was supplied, so the general US federal statutory rate of 21.0% is used, which is also the rate behind the filed NOPAT and ROIC series. The stress margin of 22% is below both the 28.7% current and 26.0% median margins and near the 21.2% actually filed in FY2024.

provisionalLabels.gate1HistoryInsufficientYears: Red-team judgment with no observations (Appendix B). Direction of error is suppression, so a wrong threshold shows less rather than something false (§6.2).
provisionalLabels.gate1ShortHistoryYears: Red-team judgment with no observations (Appendix B), same basis as the <5-year threshold (§6.2).
